one_sentence_story: Searching for a zero-bias baseline at Bristol in 1971, Holocaust survivor Henri Tajfel discovered the Minimal Group Effect — assigning boys randomly to 'Klee' or 'Kandinsky' painting groups with zero contact or self-benefit caused them to sacrifice total group wealth (picking 7-vs-1 over 19-vs-25) simply so 'Us' came out ahead of 'Them'.
so_what_for_you: Audit every label you hand out at work or school: arbitrary silos ('Day Shift vs Night Shift', 'HQ vs Field') automatically breed zero-sum 7-vs-1 turf wars — unite people in **cross-cutting, shared-goal teams** so 'Us' expands.

jargon_map.plain: stripping groups down to nothing but an arbitrary label (Klee vs Kandinsky), anonymity, and zero self-profit — yet still observing robust in-group favoritism
jargon_map.analogy: finding sparks inside an empty test tube

jargon_map.term: Maximum Difference (7/1) vs Maximum Joint Profit (19/25)
jargon_map.plain: Tajfel's matrix trap proving people sacrifice total wealth and even their own group's absolute payout just to rank higher than the out-group
jargon_map.analogy: preferring $7 when rivals get $1 over $19 when rivals get $25

jargon_map.plain: principle that part of our self-esteem comes from the groups we belong to — pushing us to make 'our group' positively distinct
jargon_map.analogy: polishing our team trophy to feel taller ourselves

jargon_map.term: in-group love vs out-group hate asymmetry
jargon_map.plain: finding that minimal labels readily trigger unequal *helping/rewards* for 'Us' while resisting direct *cruelty* unless threat is added
jargon_map.analogy: cheering louder for home jerseys without wanting rivals hurt

jargon_map.plain: merging rival 'Klee' and 'Kandinsky' sub-tribes under one shared mission identity ('Common Ingroup Identity', Gaertner & Dovidio)
jargon_map.analogy: rival club players putting on the same national team jersey
